newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee steady vs spot, gains vs forward dlr.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee steady vs spot, gains vs forward dlr.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed steady against the dollar in the spot and ended up against the forward dollar on Friday despite political uncertainties, dealers said.
The spot rupee closed steady at 35.84/85 against the dollar.
The spot market was dull and inactive in thin trade with the rupee stuck at 35.84 level, dealers said. Most of the deals were at 35.84 with stray deals at 35.8375, they said.
The rupee opened mildly weak against the forward dollar largely on political worries but ended up in the absence of the expected importer covering, dealers said.

October dollars closed at 1.20/1.22 rupees compared to the day's opening level of 1.27/1.30 rupees. The six month annualised premium closed Friday at 6.19 percent compared with the previous close of 6.36 percent.
The political drama unfolding in New Delhi had little impact on the rupee, dealers said. The ruling United Front government faces a confidence vote in the parliament on Friday night.
"Importers continue to be uncovered and exporters sold (their dollar receivables)," said a bank dealer.
"Politics has already been discounted for," said another dealer. He said the market was looking forward to the central bank's credit policy due on April 15 rather than the developments in Delhi.
